1.explanation: To add a new ‘apex’ language, you must (1) register it in components.js under components.languages so the core build knows about prism-apex.js; (2) add an entry in prism-autoloader’s lang_dependencies (so 'apex' points at 'java' or 'clike') and in lang_aliases (so alias 'apex' resolves correctly) to enable lazy-loading; (3) include prism-apex.js in the build by updating gulpfile.js/paths.js (components and/or plugins arrays). The loadLanguages and loadLanguage functions orchestrate loading grammars, so they will pick up the new mappings once you’ve updated the dependency and alias tables.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows a Salesforce Apex code snippet (e.g. List<Contact> contacts = [ SELECT Id, AccountId FROM Contact]; … ) but Prism is treating it as Java. Even if you alias “apex” to the Java grammar, the Display-language plugin still shows the label “Java” instead of “Apex”. The goal is to add first-class support for Apex: load the Java grammar under the name “apex” and have the correct label.

2.explanation: To teach Prism about Apex you must: 1) In components.js under the “languages” map, add an entry for “apex” (so the autoloader knows there is a prism-apex component). 2) In prism-autoloader.js extend the lang_dependencies object so that loading “apex” will pull in the Java grammar, and add an alias in lang_aliases so that ‘apex’ resolves to ‘java’. 3) In gulpfile.js/paths.js add your new prism-apex.js file to the components (or main) arrays so it gets picked up by the build. Without these changes Prism won’t recognize “apex” as a language key, won’t load its script, and will never alias it to Java’s grammar for highlighting.
2.bug_scenario: The user wants to add syntax‐highlighting support for Apex (Salesforce’s Java‐like language) to Prism. In the screenshot you can see Apex code (List<Contact> contacts = …) rendered without any Java/Apex highlighting, because Prism doesn’t know about “apex” as a language. You need to alias or wire “apex” to the existing Java grammar so that Prism will highlight Apex code the same way it does Java.
